name: Barry Goldwater
role: US Senator from Arizona (1953-1965, 1969-1987); Republican presidential nominee 1964
summary: Goldwater was the leading American movement conservative of his day. He argued for limited, constitutionally bound government, ending farm subsidies and graduated income taxes, state right-to-work laws and private rather than federal welfare. He opposed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 on constitutional grounds while saying he opposed segregation, wanted military superiority over the Soviet Union, voted against the 1963 test ban treaty, and in 1993 backed gay service in the military.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He called the US military establishment necessary and deplored the prospect of conquest that its absence would bring.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: He wrote that the principle of an equal percentage claim holds equally with regard to incomes, accepting an income tax at a single rate.

arms-reduction.rationale: He wrote that no nation in its right mind gives up the means of defence and that he opposed 'economizing' on the nation's safety.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He wrote that cutting taxes before firm decisions on spending would 'court deficit spending and the inflationary effects that invariably follow'.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He wrote 'Let welfare be a private concern' and that private charity is better than government welfare.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He wrote that employees have a right to select a common agent to bargain with their employer, and that collective bargaining works for the common good when confined to the employer and its employees.

collective-defense.rationale: In 1964 he called NATO 'the greatest bulwark ever erected by free nations'.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He wrote that the framers' system of restraints was directed against a 'tyranny of the masses' as well as individual tyrants.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He opposed the government taking responsibility for citizens' needs 'from cradle to grave' and said welfare should be private, or state and local if public.

decide-locally.rationale: He argued that the states keep all powers not delegated, that education problems belong to localities, and that any public welfare should be done by 'local and state authorities'.

defeat-communism.rationale: He wrote that the objective is 'victory over Communism' and that peaceful coexistence is an assumption made 'at the risk of losing our national life'.

democracy-best.rationale: He wrote that the framers did not create a democracy but a republic with restraints directed against 'a tyranny of the masses'.

economic-freedom.rationale: He wrote that a man's 'political freedom is illusory if he is dependent for his economic needs on the State' and that no one can be economically free if enslaved politically.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He argued that the US should re-examine its UN commitment and that its interests usually suffer when it subordinates its policy to the UN.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: In 1964 he called NATO 'the greatest bulwark ever erected by free nations' and attacked the administration for undermining it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He wrote that the framers put certain activities outside the legitimate scope of public authority and that change must go through the Article V amendment procedure.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He quoted the 1866 Civil Rights Act and the Fourteenth Amendment as giving all persons, Negroes included, a civil right to equal benefit of all laws.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He wrote that an egalitarian society 'does violence both to the charter of the Republic and the laws of Nature' and that artificial devices for enforcing equality must be rejected.

farm-price-support.rationale: He called for 'prompt and final termination of the farm subsidy program' and for ending price supports.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He wrote that government has a right to claim an equal percentage of each man's wealth and no more, and that the principle holds equally for incomes.

force-without-un.rationale: He argued that US policy should not be subordinated to the UN and that the Security Council and Assembly often work against US aims.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: He wrote that America should come to the aid of captive peoples who want to strike out for freedom and called for an 'offensive-minded strategy' against Communism.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He opposed suspending US nuclear tests and called for superiority in all weapons, nuclear ones included.

industrial-unions.rationale: He wrote that the evil to be eliminated is the power to enforce industry-wide bargaining and that employees should deal with their own employer.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He opposed suspending US nuclear tests and called for superiority in all weapons against Communist powers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He wrote that production, farm production included, 'is best controlled by the natural operation of the free market' and urged ending farm subsidies so that the laws of economics decide.

military-superiority.rationale: He called for 'superiority in all of the weapons' and said he would spend what it takes and was not in favor of 'economizing' on the nation's safety.

nation-first.rationale: He wrote that when US policy is subordinated to the UN its national interest usually suffers, and that foreign aid is unconstitutional except as it promotes America's national interests.

national-mission.rationale: In 1964 he said Americans 'can be freedom's missionaries in a doubting world'.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He praised free enterprise as the basis of freedom and opposed collectivism and Communism alike.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He wrote that government has legitimate functions delegated by the Constitution, taxed at an equal percentage, covering more than protection from violence, such as national defence.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He wrote that those who are fortunate and able should be encouraged to care for the unfortunate and disabled, through private charity.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: In 1993 he wrote that it is 'high time to pull the curtains on this charade of policy' and that the ban on gays in the military is senseless.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He wrote that the framers declared certain activities outside the legitimate scope of public authority and divided power, so that no body is supreme.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He wrote that the proper function of the school is to transmit the cultural heritage of one generation to the next, and faulted schools for neglecting it.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: In 1964 he said America must look beyond the defense of freedom today to its extension tomorrow and be 'freedom's missionaries'.

property-fundamental.rationale: He wrote that each man has an inalienable right to his property, and in 1964 called 'the sanctity of private property the only durable foundation for constitutional government in a free society'.

public-ownership.rationale: He described a 'State owned and operated economy' as the collectivist threat to freedom and said the evils of nationalization are self-evident.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In his 1964 Senate speech he said he was 'unalterably opposed to discrimination or segregation on the basis of race, color, or creed'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He deplored the 'maze of government regulations' on the businessman; the only controls on corporations he endorsed were the antitrust laws against monopoly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He wrote that the US government has no 'right, much less the obligation, to try to promote the economic and social welfare of foreign peoples' and that foreign aid cannot be defended as charity.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He wrote that foreign aid has created anti-Americanism among 'proud peoples' who resent dependence on a foreign dole.

separated-powers.rationale: He wrote that the framers dispersed public authority among levels and branches so that each would resist aggression by the others, and he deplored the decay of that 'system of restraints'.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He wanted the US to lead the free world against the Communist bloc and said the strong can keep the peace.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He called the graduated income tax 'confiscatory', said he does not believe in punishing success, and called for abolishing its graduated features.

unions-good.rationale: He wrote that unionism kept within its proper bounds 'accomplishes a positive good' and can be an instrument of economic justice for the working man, while attacking compulsory membership, union politics and industry-wide bargaining.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He wrote that he sees no moral virtue in voting for 'free medical care' funded by taxing others, and that welfare should be a private concern, or, if public, a local and state one, not a federal one.

voluntary-union-payments-at-work.rationale: He strongly favored state right-to-work laws that forbid contracts making union membership a condition of employment.

notes: Most answers rest on The Conscience of a Conservative (1960), published under his name and ghostwritten by L. Brent Bozell; it is used as his stated position. His 1964 speech and 1993 op-ed are third-party copies of the originals.
